x: Barnet had their new star, Ron Higgs, and did just enough to take gold, which of course was much commented upon afterwards by Bob Belmore. Bob Treadwell had rested from the National at Parliament Hill the previous week in anticipation of the strong field and the demanding course.

There had even been selection problems with Pat Newell running into form in the VAC '10' the week before and getting the verdict over a slightly less fit Bert Stroud. Barnet played their trump card on the opening stage by running Ron Higgs. He had a blinding run, setting a new record time of 17:27.

He stormed round in 21:39 to overtake TVH but Barnet, with Ron Higgs also running very well, were too strong and held on for the gold. In all an excellent day and a good practice for next May's relays which are at the same venue.
Ron Higgs who had travelled to Cardiff with Laurie and Charlie also ran very well and was delighted to finish in third place in front of Maurice Morrell.
